Trademarks

FAQ on Trademarks

Common questions we hear from clients considering their first — or fifth — trademark filing.

Words, logos, slogans, and in some cases sounds, colours, or packaging shapes — provided the mark can distinguish your goods or services from others in the marketplace.
An uncontested application typically clears examination and publication within 12–18 months, though timelines depend on Registry workload and whether objections or oppositions are raised.
"TM" can be used with any mark you're using in commerce, registered or not. The ® symbol may only be used once the mark is formally registered with the Trade Marks Registry.
Yes — use creates common-law rights and can support a "prior use" claim, but those rights are narrower and harder to enforce than a granted registration.
A third party can oppose within four months of publication in the Trademark Journal. You'll file a counter-statement, both sides submit evidence, and the Registry decides after a hearing — see our Trademark Opposition page.
Yes — registration lasts 10 years and must be renewed thereafter in further 10-year terms, indefinitely, as long as the mark remains in use.
Yes. Trademarks can be assigned outright or licensed for use by third parties, both of which should be formally recorded with the Registry to be fully enforceable.
No. A trademark protects brand identifiers used in commerce; copyright protects original creative works such as text, art, and software. A logo can sometimes attract both forms of protection at once.
No — Indian registration only protects the mark within India. International protection requires separate filings, or a Madrid Protocol application designating the countries you need. See our Global Network page.
These answers are general information, not legal advice for your specific situation. Trademark strategy should account for the particular facts of your mark, industry, and markets.
